laneBSuccessorWave20260818.requiredGate: One mounted, production-path test on real PostgreSQL, using the SAME signed token throughout: (1) issue one genuinely signed token (jsonwebtoken, HS256, real JWT_SECRET, no jti so token-revocation lookup is a pure pass-through) for a user whose organization_members row is ACTIVE; drive a real business GET through the actual mounted Gateway chain (gatewayVerifyToken + requireActiveAuditsMembership + the real audits router, not a test-only Express app re-wiring the same middleware by hand) and assert success with real business data. (3) issue the very next request with the identical token and assert the EXACT denial: 403, body {error: 'You no longer have access to this organization', code: 'ORG_MEMBERSHIP_REVOKED'} — this is the literal output of the deny() helper in auditsStrictMembership.middleware.ts, which requireActiveAuditsMembership uses on every non-ACTIVE status with no caching (the module re-reads organization_members on every single request by design, per its own header comment). AND organization_id = ?` on every single request with no cache layer — this is called out explicitly in the module's own header comment as the deliberate difference from the general-purpose validateOrgMembership (60s cache, fail-open on DB error). This is exactly why the required gate's step 3 (very next request denies) is expected to work: there is no cache window to wait out.
wireDiscoveredButNotYetRun.mountPoint: Gateway.ts:1331 — app.use('/api/audits', gatewayVerifyToken, auditsStrictMembership, auditsMethodRouter) — this is the real production mount this gate must drive a supertest request through, not a hand-rolled Express app that re-attaches the same middleware functions in a different wiring.
wireDiscoveredButNotYetRun.orgFallbackWrinkle: auth.middleware.ts's attachUser has a deliberate rescue: if the token's resolved organization is NOT an ACTIVE membership for the user, it searches for ANY OTHER ACTIVE org for that user and silently switches req.organizationId to it (comment-labeled 'BUG-02/15' rescue). This means the test fixture MUST give the token-holder exactly ONE organization_members row (the one that gets revoked) — if the user had a second ACTIVE membership elsewhere, step 3 would silently switch tenants and pass instead of deny, which would be a false negative for this exact gate. This wrinkle is the reason a naively-written version of this test could pass for the wrong reason, and is being recorded here before the test is written so the fixture design is auditable independent of the result.
wireDiscoveredButNotYetRun.jtiOmission: The signed test token must omit the jti claim (or use one not present in revoked_tokens) — checkTokenRevocation short-circuits to attachUser immediately when no jti is present, keeping the token-revocation check (a different, unrelated mechanism) out of this test's causal path.
